==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑːdɪnəl ˈnjuːməɹəl/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-cardinal numeral.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑɹdɪnəl ˈnumɜɹəl/|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|grammar}} A word used to represent a [[cardinal number]].
#* {{RQ:New World of English Words|edition=6th|entry=Numerals|page=463|column=1|passage='''''Cardinal Numerals''''', are thoſe which expreſs the Number of things, as ''One'', ''Two'', ''Three'', ''Four''; [...]}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1993|author=William W. Derbyshire|title=A Basic Reference Grammar of Slovene|publisher=Columbus, Ohio: Slavica Publishers, Inc.|page=56
|passage=The '''cardinal numeral''' ‘one’ occurs in the singular and is declined like ''bogàt''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Laurie Bauer; Rodney Huddleston|chapter=Lexical word-formation|title=The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language|page=1716
|passage=Numerals cut across the division between syntax and morphology: '''cardinal numerals''' expressing numbers below 100 are single words, while those expressing higher numbers are syntactically composite.}}
